findings.chem6_is_per_track: VERIFIED from chem6_10keV.mac (/gun/position 0 0 0, one e- per event) - chemistry is per-event, so our per-primary IRT IS the correct comparison. Geometry ruled out.
findings.reactions_rise_uniformly: All 9 reactions rise ~1.4x with the cascade (not one channel) - a general over-density, ~density^2 for 1.22x more radicals.
findings.fewer_radicals_more_recomb: Our tertiary dump has FEWER radicals than Geant4 (459 vs 509 ions/pri) yet MORE recombination -> our radicals are packed tighter than Geant4 effectively.
findings.irt_sampling_faithful: Our sampleIRT (type0/type1) has the correct diffusion-escape probability (Winf=sigma/r0e, erfcinv) - the per-pair sampling is a faithful G4DNAIRT port.
findings.placement_geometry_CORRECTION: RETRACTED 2026-06-09: my first claim (Geant4 anti-correlates ionisation products) was WRONG. Read the source carefully: for Ionisation_DissociationDecay, Geant4 gives ONE of {OH, H3O+} a 0.8nm random-direction displacement and leaves the other at the mother site (2.0nm) — EXACTLY what our worker does. The anti-correlated 0.5/-0.5 spreading is for the B1A1/A1B1 EXCITATION channels, not ionisation. So ionisation placement MATCHES Geant4 and is NOT the cause. (Caught by verify-before-asserting before any fix was built on it.)
findings.refined_open_question: Verified NOT the cause: chem6 geometry, sampleIRT, ionisation product placement. What remains: Geant4 has MORE radicals than us (509 ionisations vs our 412) yet LESS recombination -> Geant4's cascade radicals are more spatially SPREAD than ours. The real difference is the spatial spread of the secondary/tertiary cascade (electron travel distances + eaq thermalisation placement), NOT the per-ionisation product displacement. This is re-opened and not yet pinned to a specific line — needs a direct measurement of the radical spatial spread (ours vs the chem6/Geant4 chemistry-stage positions), which dnaphysics' physics-stage ntuple does not directly provide.
